input.quote: MSL agrees to protect, defend, hold harmless, and indemnify IBM from and against any and all claims, damages, liabilities, losses and expenses, arising out of the following, whether alleged or actual:
input.rationale: Section 15.1 contains a genuine vendor-side indemnity running to us: MSL defends and indemnifies IBM for (a) infringement of any patent, trademark, trade name, copyright, mask work right or trade secret anywhere in the world arising from MSL's performance or MSL-procured parts, processes, designs and pre-existing materials, (b) MSL's failure to comply with law, and (c) MSL's failure to perform its warranty and support obligations. The carve-outs are the usual ones (IBM-selected names/marks, MSL's compliance with IBM's written specifications, defects caused by IBM-supplied designs), and 15.2 supplies standard procedure (prompt notice, cooperation, MSL control with our right to participate at our own expense) plus the customary procure-a-licence/redesign remedy in 15.2(b). Section 14 of the Equipment and Program Loan Agreement is a narrow, loaned-item-only IBM obligation, so there is no broad reciprocal customer indemnity. The clause therefore meets the fallback and substantially the preferred position. Minor sub-elements short of preferred (no express extension to IBM affiliates, no separate limbs for data breach or gross negligence/wilful misconduct, no refund remedy) are noted only. Separately, the 3%-of-bill-of-materials cap in 15.3(b) is expressed to cover "total liability ... regardless of the form of action" and so would bite on this indemnity; that is a limitation-of-liability point and is addressed under the liability rule rather than double-flagged here.
